author: Mary Oliver
citation: Why I Wake Early (2004) · "Mindful"

text: My work is loving the world. Here the sunflowers, there the hummingbird — equal seekers of sweetness.
author: Mary Oliver
citation: Thirst (2006) · "Messenger"

text: Someone I loved once gave me a box full of darkness. It took me years to understand that this, too, was a gift.
author: Mary Oliver
citation: Thirst (2006) · "The Uses of Sorrow"

text:
Instructions for living a life:
Pay attention.
Be astonished.
Tell about it.
author: Mary Oliver
citation: Red Bird (2008) · "Sometimes", § 4

text:
Among the swans there is none called the least,
or the greatest.
author: Mary Oliver
citation: Evidence (2009) · "Evidence"

text: I believe in kindness. Also in mischief. Also in singing, especially when singing is not necessarily prescribed.
author: Mary Oliver
citation: Evidence (2009) · "Evidence"

text: Keep some room in your heart for the unimaginable.
author: Mary Oliver
citation: Evidence (2009) · "Evidence"

text: We all need to be reminded and encouraged to relax with whatever arises and bring whatever we encounter to the path.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

text: Fear is a natural reaction to moving closer to the truth.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

text: Life is a good teacher and a good friend. Things are always in transition, if we could only realize it.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

text: This very moment is the perfect teacher, and, lucky for us, it’s with us wherever we are.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

text: Meditation is just gently coming back again and again to what’s right here.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: How to Meditate: A Practical Guide to Making Friends with Your Mind (2008)

text: We can’t control what’s going to happen but we can grow in awareness of what is happening.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: How to Meditate: A Practical Guide to Making Friends with Your Mind (2008)

text: The experience of a sad and tender heart is what gives birth to fearlessness.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: How to Meditate: A Practical Guide to Making Friends with Your Mind (2008)

text: This is a standard meditation instruction that you can embody in the entirety of your life: do not act out and do not repress. See what happens if you don’t do either of those things.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: How to Meditate: A Practical Guide to Making Friends with Your Mind (2008)

text: What other people label or might try to call failure, I have learned is just God’s way of pointing you in a new direction.
author: Oprah Winfrey
citation: 2005–2008 · Oprah's commencement speech at Howard University (May 12, 2007)

text: Turn your wounds into wisdom.
author: Oprah Winfrey
citation: 2011–2019 · CNN interview (2011) · OWN Network on "Oprah Winfrey Show"

text: Nourish what makes you feel confident, connected, contented. Opportunity will rise to meet you.
author: Oprah Winfrey
citation: 2011–2019 · The Path Made Clear: Discovering Your Life's Direction and Purpose (2019) · p. 188

text: Laughter is carbonated holiness.
author: Anne Lamott
citation: Plan B

text: Lighthouses don’t go running all over an island looking for boats to save; they just stand there shining.
author: Anne Lamott
citation: Bird by Bird

text: The game of life is hard, and a lot of us are playing hurt.
author: Anne Lamott
citation: "The dressing-room encounter that made me get real about aging" The Washington Post (December 20, 2023)

text: We know by a certain age the great palace lies of the culture — if you buy or do or achieve this or that, you will be happy and rich. Nope. Love and service make us rich.
author: Anne Lamott
citation: "The dressing-room encounter that made me get real about aging" The Washington Post (December 20, 2023)

text: Sometimes I feel this summer as if I were walking through the green meadow again; idly, aimlessly, unthinking, and unguided.
author: Kate Chopin
citation: The Awakening (1899)

text:
The new dawn blooms as we free it.
For there is always light.
If only we’re brave enough to see it.
If only we’re brave enough to be it.
author: Amanda Gorman
citation: The Hill We Climb (2020)

text: Color is one of the great things in the world that makes life worth living to me and as I have come to think of painting it is my effort to create an equivalent with paint color for the world – life as I see it.
author: Georgia O'Keeffe

text: You cannot save people, you can only love them.
author: Anaïs Nin
work: The Diary of Anais Nin, Volume Two (1934-1939)
citation: Diary entries (1914-1974) · The Diary of Anais Nin, Volume Two (1934-1939)

text: Experience teaches acceptance of the imperfect as life.
author: Anaïs Nin
citation: Diary entries (1914-1974) · Feb. 15, 1936

text: Each friend represents a world in us, a world possibly not born until they arrive, and it is only by this meeting that a new world is born.
author: Anaïs Nin
citation: Diary entries (1914-1974) · March 1937

text: There are very few human beings who receive the truth, complete and staggering, by instant illumination. Most of them acquire it fragment by fragment, on a small scale, by successive developments, cellularly, like a laborious mosaic.
author: Anaïs Nin
citation: Diary entries (1914-1974) · Fall 1943

text: When I dare to be powerful, to use my strength in the service of my vision, then it becomes less and less important whether I am afraid.
author: Audre Lorde
citation: The Cancer Journals (1980)

text: We are all more blind to what we have than to what we have not.
author: Audre Lorde
work: Notes from a Trip to Russia
citation: Sister Outsider: Essays and Speeches (1984) · Notes from a Trip to Russia · p. 31

text: The need for sharing deep feeling is a human need.
author: Audre Lorde
work: Uses of the Erotic: The Erotic as Power
citation: Sister Outsider: Essays and Speeches (1984) · Uses of the Erotic: The Erotic as Power · p. 58

text: Living is like tearing through a museum. Not until later do you really start absorbing what you saw, thinking about it, looking it up in a book, and remembering — because you can’t take it all in at once.
author: Audrey Hepburn
citation: As quoted in Audrey Hepburn : A Bio-bibliography (1994) by David Hofstede

text: Success is like reaching an important birthday and finding you’re exactly the same.
author: Audrey Hepburn
work: Audrey Hepburn: A Life in Pictures
citation: As quoted in Audrey Hepburn : A Life in Pictures (2007) by Yann-Brice Dherbier and Pierre-Henri Verlhac

text: I love people who make me laugh. I honestly think it’s the thing I like most, to laugh. It cures a multitude of ills. It’s probably the most important thing in a person.
author: Audrey Hepburn
citation: How to be Lovely‎ (2005)

text: I never think of myself as an icon. What is in other people’s minds is not in my mind. I just do my thing.
author: Audrey Hepburn
citation: How to be Lovely‎ (2005) · p. 143

text: I always love it when people write me and say “I was having a rotten time, and I walked into a cinema and saw one of your movies, and it made such a difference.”
author: Audrey Hepburn
citation: How to be Lovely‎ (2005)

text: Even if the whole world were to fall to pieces, the unity of the psyche would never be shattered. And the wider and more numerous the fissures on the surface, the more the unity is strengthened in the depths.
author: Carl Jung
citation: Civilization in Transition (1964)

text: Yesterday is done. Tomorrow never comes. Today is here. If you don’t know what to do, sit still and listen.
author: Carl Sandburg
citation: Incidentals (1904)

text: I’m an idealist. I don’t know where I’m going, but I’m on my way.
author: Carl Sandburg
citation: Incidentals (1904)

text:
The fog comes
on little cat feet.
It sits looking
over the harbor and city
on silent haunches, and then moves on.
author: Carl Sandburg

text: A baby is God’s opinion that life should go on.
author: Carl Sandburg
citation: Remembrance Rock (1948), Ch. 2, p. 7

text: One of the greatest necessities in America is to discover creative solitude.
author: Carl Sandburg
work: Peter’s Quotations: Ideas for Our Time‎
citation: As quoted in Peter's Quotations: Ideas for Our Time‎ (1977) by Laurence J. Peter, p. 448

text:
You never can tell when you do an act
Just what the result will be;
But with every deed you are sowing a seed,
Though the harvest you may not see.
author: Ella Wheeler Wilcox
citation: Poetry quotes · You Never Can Tell (1895).

text:
I’m no reformer; for I see more light
Than darkness in the world; mine eyes are quick
To catch the first dim radiance of the dawn,
And slow to note the cloud that threatens storm.
author: Ella Wheeler Wilcox
citation: Poetry quotes · Poems of Pleasure (1900) · Optimism

text:
I find a rapture linked with each despair,
Well worth the price of anguish. I detect
More good than evil in humanity.
Love lights more fires than hate extinguishes,
And men grow better as the world grows old.
author: Ella Wheeler Wilcox
citation: Poetry quotes · Poems of Pleasure (1900) · Optimism

author: Ella Wheeler Wilcox
citation: Poetry quotes · New Thought Pastels (1913) · Climbing

text: To live is so startling, it leaves but little room for other occupations.
author: Emily Dickinson
citation: Letter to T. W. Higginson (late 1872); Letters (1958) p. 380, no. 381

text: We turn not older with years, but newer every day.
author: Emily Dickinson
citation: Letter to Louise Norcross (late 1872); Letters (1958) p. 499, no. 379

text:
I’m Nobody! Who are you?
Are you – Nobody – Too?
author: Emily Dickinson
citation: Poems · I'm Nobody! Who are you? (J)

text:
A Vastness, as a Neighbor, came,
A Wisdom, without Face, or Name,
A Peace, as Hemispheres at Home
And so the Night became.
author: Emily Dickinson
citation: Poems · The Crickets sang (J)

text: I tell you: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
citation: Thus Spoke Zarathustra (1883) · Prologue, § 5

text: There is more wisdom in your body than in your deepest philosophy.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
citation: Thus Spoke Zarathustra (1883) · Part I, Chapter 4

text: Whence come the highest mountains? I once asked. Then I learned that they came out of the sea. The evidence is written in their rocks and in the walls of their peaks. It is out of the deepest depth that the highest must come to its height.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
citation: Thus Spoke Zarathustra (1883) · Part III, Chapter 45

text: Mature manhood: that means to have rediscovered the seriousness one had as a child at play.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
citation: Beyond Good and Evil (1886) · Chapter IV, aphorism 94, tr. R. J. Hollingdale

text: It is impossible to live without failing at something, unless you live so cautiously that you might as well not have lived at all – in which case, you fail by default.
author: J. K. Rowling
citation: 2008 · Harvard address (2008)

text: The world is full of wonderful things you haven’t seen yet. Don’t ever give up on the chance of seeing them.
author: J. K. Rowling
citation: 2015 · Online tweet, in response to an extremely depressed person contemplating suicide, as quoted in Alex Ungerman "J.K. Rowling Sends Beautiful Message to Fan Who Wants to 'Finally Give Up'", ET Online (5 May 2015).

text: Far away in the sunshine are my highest aspirations. I may not reach them, but I can look up and see their beauty, believe in them, and try to follow where they lead.
author: Louisa May Alcott
citation: As quoted in Elbert Hubbard's Scrap Book (1923) by Elbert Hubbard, p. 62

text: Lovely weather so far; I don’t know how long it will last, but I’m not afraid of storms, for I’m learning how to sail my ship.
author: Louisa May Alcott
citation: Little Women (1868) · Amy, in Ch. 44 : My Lord and Lady; part of this has sometimes been slightly misquoted as: "I am not afraid of storms, for I am learning how to sail my ship."

text: I had a pleasant time with my mind, for it was happy.
author: Louisa May Alcott
citation: Life, Letters, and Journals. (1898) · Early Diary kept at Fruitlands, 1843.

text: You did in your twenties what you knew how to do, and when you knew better you did better. And you should not be judged for the person that you were, but for the person that you’re trying to be and the woman that you are now.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: As quoted by Oprah Winfrey. · Oprah Winfrey quoted this from a personal conversation with her friend, Maya Angelou.

text: You may not control all the events that happen to you, but you can decide not to be reduced by them.
author: Maya Angelou
work: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
citation: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings (1969) · Letter to my daughter quotes(September 19, 2026)

text: We may encounter many defeats, but we must not be defeated.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings (1969) · Maya Angelou quotes qfp( September 19, 2026)

text:
You may write me down in history
With your bitter, twisted lies,
You may trod me in the very dirt
But still, like dust, I’ll rise.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: And Still I Rise (1978) · "Still I Rise" - Full text online at poets.org

text:
We grow despite the
horror that we feed
upon our own
tomorrow.
We grow.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: I Shall Not Be Moved (1990) · "Glory Falls"

text: If we are bold, love strikes away the chains of fear from our souls.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: A Brave and Startling Truth (1995)

text:
We, unaccustomed to courage
exiles from delight
live coiled in shells of loneliness
until love leaves its high holy temple
and comes into our sight
to liberate us into life.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: A Brave and Startling Truth (1995)

text:
When we come to it
We must confess that we are the possible
We are the miraculous, the true wonders of this world
That is when, and only when
We come to it.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: A Brave and Startling Truth (1995)

text: I know when it’s the best I can do. It may not be the best there is. Another writer may do it much better. But I know when it’s the best I can do.
author: Maya Angelou
citation: Paris Review Interview (1990)

text: The world always seems brighter when you’ve just made something that wasn’t there before.
author: Neil Gaiman
citation: 2004 · "Gunpowder treason and plot" Blog entry (5 Nov 2004)

text: “Because,” she said, “when you’re scared but you still do it anyway, that’s brave.”
author: Neil Gaiman
citation: Book quotes · Coraline (2002)

text: The world doesn’t have to be like this. Things can be different.
author: Neil Gaiman
citation: Book quotes · Why our future depends on libraries, reading and daydreaming (2013)

text: Honestly, if you’re given the choice between Armageddon or tea, you don’t say “what kind of tea?”
author: Neil Gaiman
citation: 2009 · In a widely reported post from his Twitter account (25 February 2009)

text: Why do I have this imagination? It’s the only one I’ve got!
author: Neil Gaiman
citation: 2007 · San Diego Comicon (2007)

text: It is a little dark still, but there are warnings of the day and somewhere out of the darkness a bird is singing to the Dawn.
author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
citation: Representative American Negroes, an essay from The Negro Problem, a collection of essays written in 1903 by leading African Americans.

text:
An angel, robed in spotless white,
Bent down and kissed the sleeping Night.
Night woke to blush; the sprite was gone.
Men saw the blush and called it Dawn.
author: Paul Laurence Dunbar

text: Blest hour! it was a luxury — to be!
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
citation: "Reflections on Having Left a Place of Retirement", l. 43 (1795)

text: In nature there is nothing melancholy.
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
citation: The Nightingale: A Conversation Poem, ll. 13-22 (1798)

text: Joy rises in me, like a summer’s morn.
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
citation: "A Christmas Carol", st. viii (1799)

text:
Tranquillity! thou better name
Than all the family of Fame!
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
citation: "Ode to Tranquillity", st. 1 (1801)

text:
Sea, and hill, and wood,
With all the numberless goings-on of life,
Inaudible as dreams!
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
citation: "Frost at Midnight", l. 11 (1798)

text:
Joy is the sweet voice, Joy the luminous cloud —
We in ourselves rejoice!
And thence flows all that charms or ear or sight,
All melodies the echoes of that voice,
All colours a suffusion from that light.
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
citation: Dejection: An Ode (1802) · St. 5

text:
Oh, is it not enough to be
Here with this beauty over me?
My throat should ache with praise, and I
Should kneel in joy beneath the sky.
Oh, beauty are you not enough?
author: Sara Teasdale
citation: Rivers to the Sea (1915) · "Spring Night"

text:
Life has loveliness to sell,
All beautiful and splendid things,
Blue waves whitened on a cliff,
Soaring fire that sways and sings,
And children’s faces looking up
Holding wonder like a cup.
author: Sara Teasdale
citation: Love Songs (1917) · "Barter"

text:
Spend all you have for loveliness,
Buy it and never count the cost;
For one white singing hour of peace
Count many a year of strife well lost,
And for a breath of ecstasy
Give all you have been, or could be.
author: Sara Teasdale
citation: Love Songs (1917) · "Barter"

text:
O lovely chance, what can I do
To give my gratefulness to you?
You rise between myself and me
With a wise persistency;
I would have broken body and soul,
But by your grace, still I am whole.
author: Sara Teasdale
citation: Flame and Shadow (1920) · "Lovely Chance"

text:
The window-lights, myriads and myriads,
Bloom from the walls like climbing flowers.
author: Sara Teasdale
citation: Flame and Shadow (1920) · "Evening: New York"

text:
If I am peaceful, I shall see
Beauty’s face continually;
Feeding on her wine and bread
I shall be wholly comforted,
For she can make one day for me
Rich as my lost eternity.
author: Sara Teasdale
citation: Flame and Shadow (1920) · "The Wind in the Hemlock"

text:
I’d rather be my honest self
Than any made-up daisy.
author: Sarah Orne Jewett
citation: "Discontent", in St. Nicholas Magazine, Vol. 3 (February 1876), p. 247

text:
Look bravely up into the sky,
And be content with knowing
That God wished for a buttercup
Just here, where you are growing.
author: Sarah Orne Jewett
citation: "Discontent", in St. Nicholas Magazine, Vol. 3 (February 1876), p. 247

text: ‘Tain’t worthwhile to wear a day all out before it comes.
author: Sarah Orne Jewett
work: The Country of the Pointed Firs
citation: The Country of the Pointed Firs (1896) · Ch. 16

text: There must be quite a few things a hot bath won’t cure, but I don’t know many of them.
author: Sylvia Plath
citation: The Bell Jar (1963) · Ch. 2

text: I never feel so much myself as when I’m in a hot bath.
author: Sylvia Plath
citation: The Bell Jar (1963) · Ch. 2

text: I took a deep breath and listened to the old brag of my heart: I am, I am, I am.
author: Sylvia Plath
citation: The Bell Jar (1963) · Ch. 20

text: The only man who makes no mistakes is the man who never does anything.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
citation: 1900s · As quoted by Jacob A. Riis in Theodore Roosevelt, the Citizen (1904), chapter XVI A Young Men's Hero

text: There were all kinds of things I was afraid of at first, ranging from grizzly bears to ‘mean’ horses and gun-fighters; but by acting as if I was not afraid I gradually ceased to be afraid.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
citation: 1910s · Theodore Roosevelt — An Autobiography (1913) · Chapter II The Vigor of Life

text: There are many kinds of success in life worth having.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
citation: 1910s · Theodore Roosevelt — An Autobiography (1913) · Ch. IX : Outdoors and Indoors, p. 336; the final statement "quoted by Squire Bill Widener" as well as variants of it, are often misattributed to Roosevelt himself. · Variant: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.

text: Our words must be judged by our deeds; and in striving for a lofty ideal we must use practical methods; and if we cannot attain all at one leap, we must advance towards it step by step, reasonably content so long as we do actually make some progress in the right direction.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
citation: 1910s · Nobel lecture (1910)

text: Success does not lie entirely in the hands of any one of us.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
citation: 1900s · Address at the Prize Day Exercises at Groton School (1904)

text: To love or to have loved, that is enough. Ask nothing further. There is no other pearl to be found in the dark folds of life. To love is a consummation.
author: Victor Hugo
citation: Les Misérables (1862), page 1190, as translated by Charles Wilbour and provided by A.L. Bert Publishers. Source: Shawn Thomas (June 24, 2013): Quotes & Illustrations From Victor Hugo’s Les Miserables. Archived from the original on March 11, 2023.

text:
I come into the presence of still water.
And I feel above me the day-blind stars
waiting with their light. For a time
I rest in the grace of the world, and am free.
author: Wendell Berry
citation: "The Peace of Wild Things" in Green River Review, No. 1 (1968)

text:
Ask the world to reveal its quietude —
not the silence of machines when they are still,
but the true quiet by which birdsongs,
trees, bellworts, snails, clouds, storms
become what they are, and are nothing else.
author: Wendell Berry
citation: Given (2005) · Sabbaths 2001

text:
Sit and be still
until in the time
of no rain you hear
beneath the dry wind’s
commotion in the trees
the sound of flowing
water among the rocks,
a stream unheard before,
and you are where
breathing is prayer.
author: Wendell Berry
citation: Given (2005) · Sabbaths 2001

text:
Laugh.
Laughter is immeasurable. Be joyful
though you have considered all the facts.
author: Wendell Berry
citation: Poems · "Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front" in Farming: A Hand Book (1970)

text: Think in the morning. Act in the noon. Eat in the evening. Sleep in the night.
author: William Blake
citation: 1790s · The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790–1793) · Proverbs of Hell · Line 41

text:
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand
And Eternity in an hour.
author: William Blake
citation: 1800s · Auguries of Innocence (1803) · Line 1

text:
Man was made for joy and woe,
And when this we rightly know
Through the world we safely go.
Joy and woe are woven fine,
A clothing for the soul divine.
author: William Blake
citation: 1800s · Auguries of Innocence (1803) · Line 56. Compare Psalm 30:5 (KJV): "weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning."

text:
Every tear from every eye
Becomes a babe in eternity.
author: William Blake
citation: 1800s · Auguries of Innocence (1803) · Line 67

text:
He who binds to himself a joy
Does the wingèd life destroy;
But he who kisses the joy as it flies
Lives in eternity’s sunrise.
author: William Blake
citation: 1790s · Poems from Blake's Notebook (c. 1791-1792) · Several Questions Answered · No. 1, He Who Binds

text:
Can I see another’s woe,
And not be in sorrow too?
Can I see another’s grief,
And not seek for kind relief?
author: William Blake
citation: 1780s · Songs of Innocence (1789–1790) · On Another's Sorrow, st. 1

text:
When the voices of children are heard on the green
And laughing is heard on the hill,
My heart is at rest within my breast
And everything else is still.
author: William Blake
citation: 1780s · Songs of Innocence (1789–1790) · Nurse's Song, st. 1

text:
The moon like a flower
In heaven’s high bower,
With silent delight,
Sits and smiles on the night.
author: William Blake
citation: 1780s · Songs of Innocence (1789–1790) · Night, st. 1

text:
The Angel that presided o’er my birth
Said, “Little creature, formed of joy and mirth,
Go love without the help of any thing on earth.”
author: William Blake
citation: 1800s · Poems from Blake's Notebook (c. 1807-1809) · The Angel That Presided

text: Don’t shortchange the future, because of fear in the present.
author: Barack Obama
citation: 2009 · Barack Obama: "The President's News Conference With Prime Minister Gordon Brown of the United Kingdom in London, England," April 1, 2009. Online by Gerhard Peters and John T. Woolley, The American Presidency Project.

text: There’s only one thing we can be sure of, and that is the love that we have for our children, for our families, for each other. The warmth of a small child’s embrace, that is true.
author: Barack Obama
citation: 2012 · Sandy Hook Prayer Vigil (December 2012)

text: That’s where courage comes from — when we turn not from each other, or on each other, but towards one another, and we find that we do not walk alone. That’s where courage comes from.
author: Barack Obama
citation: 2013 · "Let Freedom Ring" Ceremony (August 2013)

text: Thoughts are the shadows of our feelings — always darker, emptier, simpler.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
citation: The Gay Science (1882) · Sec. 179

text: You should rather be grateful for the weeds you have in your mind, because eventually they will enrich your practice.
author: Shunryu Suzuki
citation: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970) · Right Practice · "Mind Weeds"

text: See what happens when the brain is completely still.
author: Jiddu Krishnamurti
citation: 1970s · The Urgency of Change (1970) · p. 184

text: It is impossible to enjoy idling thoroughly unless one has plenty of work to do. There is no fun in doing nothing when you have nothing to do. Wasting time is merely an occupation then, and a most exhausting one. Idleness, like kisses, to be sweet must be stolen.
author: Jerome K. Jerome
work: Idle Thoughts of an Idle Fellow
citation: Idle Thoughts of an Idle Fellow (1886) · "On Being Idle"

text: It is not when he is working in the office but when he is lying idly on the sand that his soul utters, “Life is beautiful.”
author: Lin Yutang
citation: The Importance of Living (1937) · Ch. I: The Awakening, p. 2

text: We must relearn to be alone.
author: Anne Morrow Lindbergh
citation: Gift from the Sea (1955)

text: Try to catch the voice in your head, in the very moment it complains about something. Recognise it for what it is: the voice of the ego, no more than a thought.
author: Eckhart Tolle
citation: Oneness With All Life: Inspirational Selections from A New Earth (2008)

text: Meditation is an invitation to notice when we reach our limit and to not get carried away by hope and fear.
author: Pema Chödrön
citation: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

text: Reality is always the story of a past, and what I love about the past is—it’s over.
author: Byron Katie
citation: Loving What Is: Four Questions That Can Change Your Life (2002)

text: The future is usually imagined as either better or worse than the present. If the imagined future is better, it gives you hope or pleasurable anticipation. If it is worse, it creates anxiety. Both are illusory.
author: Eckhart Tolle
citation: The Power of Now (1997)

text: Nothing we see or hear is perfect. But right there in the imperfection is perfect reality.
author: Shunryu Suzuki
work: Not Always So: Practicing the True Spirit of Zen
citation: Not Always So: Practicing the True Spirit of Zen (2002) · Wherever You Are, Enlightenment Is There (page127)

text: A man may own a thousand acres of land, and yet he still sleeps upon a bed of five feet.
author: Lin Yutang
citation: The Importance of Living (1937) · p. 38 (Chinese saying)

Can you absolutely know that it’s true?
How do you react when you believe that thought?
Who would you be without the thought?
author: Byron Katie

text:
But often faltering feet
Come surest to the goal;
And they who walk in darkness meet
The sunrise of the soul.
author: Henry Van Dyke

text: When you don’t cover up the world with words and labels, a sense of the miraculous returns to your life.

author: Eckhart Tolle

author: Epicurus

text: Remember that man lives only in the present, in this fleeting instant; all the rest of his life is either past and gone, or not yet revealed. Short, therefore, is man’s life, and narrow is the corner of the earth wherein he dwells.

author: Byron Katie

text: A cucumber is bitter. Throw it away. There are briars in the road. Turn aside from them. This is enough. Do not add, “And why were such things made in the world?”
author: Marcus Aurelius

author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: Live a balanced life — learn some and think some and draw and paint and sing and dance and play and work every day some.
author: Robert Fulghum

author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: Everywhere and at all times it is in thy power piously to acquiesce in thy present condition, and to behave justly to those who are about thee, and to exert thy skill upon thy present thoughts, that nothing shall steal into them without being well examined.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The maxim Nothing avails but perfection may be spelt shorter: ‘Paralysis.’
author: Winston Churchill

author: Bertrand Russell

author: Marcus Aurelius

text:
But two miles more, and then we rest!
Well, there is still an hour of day,
And long the brightness of the West
Will light us on our devious way;
Sit then, awhile, here in this wood—
So total is the solitude,
We safely may delay.

Toward heaven still.
And there’s a barrel that I didn’t fill
Beside it, and there may be two or three
Apples I didn’t pick upon some bough.
But I am done with apple-picking now.

text:
Hide me from day’s garish eye,
While the bee with honied thigh,
That at her flowery work doth sing,
And the waters murmuring
With such consort as they keep,
Entice the dewy-feathered sleep.

Against Heav’n’s hand or will, nor bate one jot
Of heart or hope; but still bear up, and steer
Right onward.

courage to change the things I can,

Some simple and heartfelt lay,
That shall soothe this restless feeling,
And banish the thoughts of day.

author: Vincent van Gogh

author: John Byrom
